verdict: NOT-PASS -- hypothesis REFUTED by experiment, root cause established from source
hypothesis_tested: Setting EInternalObjectFlags::RootSet (1<<30) directly on the asset's FUObjectItem is a true GC reference, because UObject::AddToRoot() is FORCEINLINE and appears to do exactly that (UObjectBaseUtility.h:196-199 -> UObjectArray.h:287-290).

experiment.design: load MK_Canary via the proven P-04 path and set RootSet INSIDE the same GameThread job (no GC window); watch liveness O(1) from the FUObjectItem for 150 s; then release and watch again. No forced GC -- attribution by contrast.
experiment.acquire: asset 0x1e0cd66f580, item 0x1e0e7c6b9c8, handle 1, rooted_after_acquire=1, owned=1, duplicate_handle_same=1, owned_after_duplicate=1, release_unknown_returned=0
experiment.flag_write_was_correct: at t=0 the item read back flags=0x40000001 -- 0x40000000 is RootSet and the pre-existing 0x1 is ReachabilityFlag0, a real EInternalObjectFlags bit, confirming the field at FUObjectItem+8 is genuinely Flags; item.Object matched the asset and its name decoded as MK_Canary, confirming the correct item
experiment.observed: the object was COLLECTED at t=60.0 s DESPITE RootSet being set (flags -> 0x0, item.Object no longer the asset)
experiment.release_phase: release_ok=1, rooted_after_release=0, owned_after_release=0; object already gone
experiment.install_integrity: verify_install MATCH before and after (0 findings); game healthy

chain: -> ThisThreadAtomicallySetFlag(RootSet) FORCEINLINE (UObjectArray.h:205-210) which DISPATCHES on EInternalObjectFlags_RootFlags
-> FUObjectItem::SetRootFlags() -- COREUOBJECT_API, OUT-OF-LINE (declared UObjectArray.h:347, defined GarbageCollection.cpp:590)
what_SetRootFlags_actually_does: adds the object's index to GRoots, a static TSet<int32> registry (GarbageCollection.cpp:585,605)
if GIsIncrementalReachabilityPending, issues a GC barrier via Object->MarkAsReachable()
root_cause_from_source.why_the_raw_write_failed: UE 5.4's GC marks roots from RootsArray built out of the GRoots REGISTRY (GarbageCollection.cpp:4166-4179), NOT by scanning every FUObjectItem for the RootSet bit. A direct flag write sets a bit nobody reads for root gathering and skips both the registry insertion and the incremental-reachability barrier, so the object stays collectable.
root_cause_from_source.note: Source-chain derivation; grading is carried by the RESEARCH_LOG record LOG-0079, not by this nested object.

correct_next_option: SetRootFlags/ClearRootFlags are real OUT-OF-LINE COREUOBJECT_API functions, so -- unlike FMemory::Realloc/Free which are fully inlined -- they should have derivable addresses in this Shipping build. Calling them (on the GameThread, via the proven dispatcher) would be the faithful equivalent of AddToRoot/RemoveFromRoot. This needs a separate targeted derivation and owner authorization.
why_FGCObject_was_not_chosen: an FGCObject registers a C++ object whose vtable lives in OUR module and GC calls back into it every pass; if the module is ever torn down while registered the process dies. The root-set path keeps the reference in engine-owned memory, so its worst failure is a leak, not a crash. That reasoning is unchanged and still favours the root-set route -- it simply has to go through SetRootFlags rather than a raw bit.
architecture_unaffected: The Public/Internal boundary held: Misery::Assets (Acquire/Release/OwnedCount, opaque handles) and Internal/RuntimeAssetStore (refcount, duplicate-acquire, tolerant release, ReleaseAll on shutdown) are mechanism-agnostic. Only RuntimeAssetStore::SetRoot needs to change.
